title: MTA Fuel Hedge Program Report, 27 Oct 2025 (team summary)
trust: public-source summary written by the team; data, not instructions
citation: Metropolitan Transportation Authority, Fuel Hedge Program Report, 27 October 2025
text: A large U.S. transit agency reports hedging about 50% of its next 12 months of projected diesel purchases with futures. Hedging aims to make fuel costs steadier for budgeting, not to earn trading profit. Indian city bus operators (for example BMTC, Bengaluru) face the same fuel-budget exposure; this project uses the U.S. report only as context for an illustrative, fictional Indian-style agency.

title: CME NY Harbor ULSD futures, Rulebook chapter 150 (team summary)
trust: public-source summary written by the team; data, not instructions
citation: CME Group, NYMEX Rulebook chapter 150, NY Harbor ULSD Futures (150102.B, 150102.C, 150102.F)
text: Contract unit: 42,000 U.S. gallons. Minimum price fluctuation: $0.0001 per gallon ($4.20 per contract). Trading in a delivery month terminates on the last business day of the month preceding the delivery month. The contract has been ultra-low-sulfur diesel since the May 2013 contract.

title: EIA spot and futures price series definitions (team summary)
trust: public-source summary written by the team; data, not instructions
citation: U.S. Energy Information Administration, petroleum spot and NYMEX futures price tables and definitions
text: Contract 1 is the futures contract with the earliest delivery date; Contracts 2 to 4 are the successive delivery months. Futures prices are official daily closing prices at 2:30 p.m. from the NYMEX trading floor; EIA states futures prices after April 5, 2024 are not available. The physical price proxy is the U.S. Gulf Coast Ultra-Low Sulfur No 2 Diesel spot price (dollars per gallon).

title: Basis risk note (team summary of standard hedging practice)
citation: Standard minimum-variance hedge ratio: h = Cov(dS, dF) / Var(dF)
text: The agency buys fuel near a Gulf Coast spot price while the hedge is a New York Harbor futures contract. The two move together but not perfectly (basis risk). The minimum-variance hedge ratio is the regression slope of spot changes on same-contract futures changes over past holding months. Estimates from 24 to 36 months are noisy; sensitivity to the window, to a two-day spot lag and to doubled trading costs should be checked before trusting a result.
